name: TSQL_STRING_CORE
signature: CONCAT(arg1, arg2, ...), CONCAT_WS(separator, arg1, arg2, ...), STRING_AGG(expr, separator) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...), LEN(expr), DATALENGTH(expr), CHARINDEX(substr, str [, start]), PATINDEX(pattern, expr), SUBSTRING(expr, start, len), STUFF(expr, start, len, replace_expr), REPLACE(expr, from_expr, to_expr)
description: Core T-SQL string processing and concatenation functions. CONCAT/CONCAT_WS are safer than '+' because they handle NULL more predictably. LEN excludes trailing spaces, while DATALENGTH returns byte count (important for NVARCHAR). CHARINDEX and PATINDEX provide 1-based position search; PATINDEX supports wildcard patterns. STRING_AGG is the primary row-to-string aggregate in SQL Server.

name: TSQL_DATETIME_CORE
signature: GETDATE(), SYSDATETIME(), DATEADD(datepart, number, date), DATEDIFF(datepart, startdate, enddate), DATETRUNC(datepart, date), EOMONTH(start_date [, month_to_add]), DATEFROMPARTS(year, month, day)
description: Core T-SQL date and time functions for arithmetic, truncation, and construction. GETDATE returns DATETIME; SYSDATETIME returns DATETIME2 with higher precision. DATEDIFF counts boundary crossings, which may differ from elapsed-duration intuition. DATETRUNC is SQL Server 2022+ and simplifies bucketed time aggregation. EOMONTH is useful for month-end calculations without manual date math.
category: T-SQL Cheat Sheet Date and Time Functions

name: TSQL_CONVERSION_CORE
signature: CAST(expr AS type), CONVERT(type, expr [, style]), TRY_CAST(expr AS type), TRY_CONVERT(type, expr [, style]), PARSE(string AS type [USING culture]), TRY_PARSE(string AS type [USING culture]), ISNULL(expr, replacement), COALESCE(expr1, expr2, ...)
description: Core T-SQL conversion and NULL-handling behavior differences. CONVERT supports style codes for date/time and character formatting (T-SQL specific). TRY_CAST and TRY_CONVERT return NULL on failure, which is useful in fuzzing pipelines to avoid hard stop. PARSE/TRY_PARSE are culture-aware but typically slower due to CLR involvement. ISNULL return type follows first argument, while COALESCE follows type precedence rules.
category: T-SQL Cheat Sheet Type Conversion and NULL Handling
